certificate_expired: SPKI SHA-256 pin {pin}; expires {expires}; the certificate isn’t valid yet or has expired: check the system clock and renew the certificate, keeping its key
certificate_expiring: SPKI SHA-256 pin {pin}; expires {expires}; it expires soon: check that the hub renews it automatically (renew a custom certificate yourself, keeping its key)
certificate_unreadable: Can’t read the certificate, or the key doesn’t match it; check ~/.persona/tls/ or public.cert_file and public.key_file. A managed certificate is made when a hub with TLS starts; the self-check doesn’t create one
config_invalid: hub.json isn’t valid JSON; fix it and run personad hub doctor again
config_unreadable: Can’t read ~/.persona/hub.json; make sure it exists and the current user can read it
credentials_mode: {path} has mode {mode} and should have {want}; run {command}
credentials_ok: Credential files in the data directory are all 0600, and credential folders closed as a whole are all 0700
credentials_windows: Skipped on Windows (POSIX permission bits don’t apply)
endpoints_none: The hub publishes no addresses; check public.advertise and the interface addresses
endpoints_ok: Read the running hub’s current list (this doesn’t mean they’re reachable from outside)
firewall_off: {command} is off or has no rules; check the host’s inbound policy and open only the hub’s TLS port to the internet
firewall_read: Read {command}; check the rules below to see whether the TLS port is open
firewall_skipped: {command} isn’t available or can’t be read, skipped (no sudo)
ipv6_none: No global IPv6 address can be confirmed as stable; check your ISP’s IPv6 and the interface addresses (only Linux reports the address flags that confirm it)
ipv6_unreadable: Can’t read the addresses; check this machine’s network interfaces
listen_invalid: No valid listen port; set listen in hub.json
listen_ok: {listen}; for the local network or a VPN only
loopback_only_off: Off: the local network and VPNs can still use the plain HTTP port with a token
loopback_only_on: On: the plain HTTP port serves only this machine; pages from the local network redirect to the TLS port and other requests get 403 tls_required
loopback_only_without_tls: On without public.tls_listen, so the hub can’t start; set a TLS listen address or turn this off
next_certificate: A browser warning about a self-signed certificate means you reached the TLS service but haven’t verified the hub’s identity yet; compare the pin in the app. If the connection times out, check the inbound IPv6 firewall and the return route through any TUN interface
next_firewall: On the host, the router and the modem, open only the hub’s TCP TLS port {port} to the internet; keep the plain HTTP port to the local network or a VPN, and check Docker’s port mappings
next_probe: On a phone with Wi-Fi off, open {url} once to test it (without a token)
proxy_protocol_idle: Applies only to the TLS port, but public.tls_listen is off, so it has no effect now
proxy_protocol_invalid: Misconfigured, so the hub can’t start: {error}
proxy_protocol_ok: Reads PROXY headers from {sources}; once it works, internet sources in the hub’s log no longer show as loopback
public_plaintext_on: Plain HTTP from the internet is on; set it to false, restart the hub and connect over HTTPS from the internet
push_bad_one: {way}; {count} device can’t get pushes or its last push didn’t go out (see below)
push_bad_other: {way}; {count} devices can’t get pushes or their last push didn’t go out (see below)
push_http: /api/v1/devices/push on this machine’s hub answered HTTP {status}; check the hub’s log
push_no_devices: {way}; no device has registered for push yet (one shows up here once you open the app on a phone and allow notifications)
push_old_hub: The running hub is too old to report each device’s push route; check again after updating it
push_reason_failed: {route}, but the last push didn’t go out ({detail})
push_reason_failed_at: {route}, but the last push at {at} didn’t go out ({detail})
push_reason_no_relay: {route}: the hub has no apns.json and the device reported no relay (the build has no relay configured, or the app is too old)
push_reason_no_token: {route}: no APNs token (the device didn’t allow notifications, or registering with APNs failed)
push_reason_relay_failed: {route}: registering with the push relay failed ({detail})
push_way_direct: The hub has its own APNs key (apns.json) and pushes straight to APNs
push_way_relay: The hub has no apns.json, so it pushes through the relay each device registered with
reach_unverified: Not verified. This machine reaches its own address over loopback, which doesn’t prove the internet can reach it.
reason_flags_unknown: the system doesn’t report the address flags or scope, so stability can’t be confirmed
route_empty: {path} has no route to check, skipped
route_ok: {source} goes through {interface}, with no sign of a TUN; still check the return path from a phone
route_query_skipped: The command isn’t available or the lookup failed, skipped
route_suspect: {source} goes through {interface}, which looks like a TUN/VPN or virtual interface; a TUN proxy may swallow replies to inbound connections (not tested). Turn off the TUN’s automatic routing or send replies to inbound connections directly, then check from a phone on cellular data
routes_not_linux: Skipped (these checks are for Linux); check them in the system’s network settings
running_http: The hub on this machine answered HTTP {status}; check that the running version, the configuration and the master token match
running_invalid: The hub on this machine answered with something invalid; check the hub’s log and the running version
running_no_token: The configuration has no master token; check token in hub.json (the self-check never creates or prints a token)
running_unreachable: Can’t connect over loopback: the hub may not be running, or not listening on loopback. Start personad hub run and check listen
title: Hub self-check (read-only)
tls_listen_invalid: No valid TLS listen port; set public.tls_listen and restart the hub
tls_listen_ok: {listen} (the configured value; TLS listening not verified)
web_push_bad_one: {count} browser was subscribed with an earlier key or its last push didn’t go out (see below)
web_push_bad_other: {count} browsers were subscribed with an earlier key or their last push didn’t go out (see below)
web_push_ok_one: {count} browser gets notifications while Persona is closed
web_push_ok_other: {count} browsers get notifications while Persona is closed
web_push_stale: {route}, but subscribed with an earlier key: it subscribes again the next time a Persona page opens in it
